t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style. A thin top bar with a wordmark. Left 40%: a checkerboard of square deep navy, limestone and white tiles bleeding off the left edge; one larger navy tile holds a white and steel-blue blueprint schematic with a thin steel-blue outline. Top right: a huge light-weight sans headline. Right 60%: option cells in a hairline grid, two above three, each with a huge light slash numeral, a short sans title and two lines of body for <CONTENT>. Flat, square corners, no shadows.
signature_idea: A Swiss checkerboard field with one blueprint tile sits beside five big slash-numbered option cells, colour on the left and reading on the right.
strengths: very close to the brand book: light huge numerals, navy/limestone blocks, square corners
option cells are clear and scannable
blueprint tile adds equipment context without clutter
maps cleanly to a token-only CSS grid
weaknesses: checkerboard is pure decoration and takes 40% of the width
white tiles add a third neutral that weakens the two-tone
stray tile numerals '01 02 02' in the blueprint tile are duplicated and mean nothing
titles with spaced colons look sloppy
invented vendor names, protocols and certifications in body copy
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone blocks, huge light slash numerals, one blueprint tile with steel-blue, hairlines and square corners match the brand book closely.
